items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Sissle also had a fine young first trumpet named Joe Keys with him.

ctx.x: There were quite a few American negros in Paris and many of them made the Hotel Liseux their meeting place. There was an American negro girl singer named Neeka Shaw who had a cabaret where a fine pianist by the name of Freddie Johnson was playing. I had heard some musicians in New York speak about Freddie Johnson and he was everything I had heard about him concerning his piano playing. Neeka's place was called the Hot Feet and was on Rue Pigalle 53.

I went to Neeka's and jammed with Freddie. One morning I met a trumpeter named Arthur Briggs in the Hot Feet but we had met before in New York when Briggs was there in 1931 with Noble Sissle at the Lafayette. Sissle also had a fine young first trumpet named Joe Keys with him.
For a young man Joe could drink more juice than any two drinking men I knew and still play his horn.
